content.title: About
content.content: Italian dressing, fat free, is a flavorful sauce made from vinegar, lemon juice, herbs, and spices, with all oils removed. It retains the classic Italian dressing taste while providing virtually no fat and very few calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The fat‑free version was created in response to growing demand for diet‑friendly condiments.
Its classic flavor comes from a blend of oregano, basil, garlic, and onion.
Mustard powder is often added to boost aroma without adding fat.
The dressing is suitable for vegetarians and vegans.
It can be used not only on salads but also as a marinade for vegetables and seafood.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: The absence of oil makes this dressing an excellent choice for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Herbs such as oregano and basil contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar and lemon juice stimulate gastric juice production, aiding food digestion.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Lemon juice provides a modest amount of vitamin C, which supports immune function.

items.title: No trans fats
items.content: Without added oils, there is no risk of consuming trans fats that can harm cardiovascular health.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions may be high in salt, which should be considered by people with hypertension.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Individuals may react to mustard, garlic, or onion.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in those with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drizzle over salads, vegetable mixes, seaweed salads, or use as a marinade for chicken, fish, and tofu. It can also be added to soups for a light tang.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in a tightly sealed container. Once opened, use within 2–3 weeks. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
